structured_output.analysis: The budget is 403/128 = 3.1484 bits per weight. The best grid, iso_3.15, measured KL=0.4361 [E514ab09c524e] at 3.14795 bits, so there are only about 0.0005 bits per weight to spare. That is far less than one layer upgrade: going from int3 to int4 (or int2 to int3) on a 3.1M-weight MLP costs about 1 bit per weight on that layer. Every loss-concentration layer has a clear upgrade gain. For example, 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 → rht_gptq_int3 0.00181 [E4c3f9b73e065, E90bd4b2f3645], and 27.up_proj gptq_int3 0.00572 → gptq_int4 0.00217 [Ef04d8aa7bded, Efea8c18d2abc]. But the only downgrades the records show cost more than the upgrades gain. For example, 27.gate_proj rht_gptq_int3 0.00499 → rht_gptq_int2 0.0234 [Efa0bb391da67, E97708161110f]. So no measured, budget-neutral layer swap is justified yet. This round I am trying changes to GPTQ options that do not change the stored bit count: act_order and damp. The prediction (0.3983) undershoots the measured 0.4361, which suggests interactions add loss and could favour error compensation that is more stable.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: This changes options only, so the stored bits stay the same and the grid stays within budget. The base iso_3.15 measured KL=0.4361 [E514ab09c524e]. Its biggest losses are in GPTQ-family MLP layers, for example 27.up_proj gptq_int3 0.00572 [Ef04d8aa7bded] and 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065]. Setting act_order=true on all GPTQ variants quantizes the columns with the most activation first.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_nonrht
proposals.rationale: This changes options only, so the bits stay the same. It sets act_order=true only for plain GPTQ (non-RHT) layers, where activation outliers are not rotated away. The plain gptq_int3 layers 27.up_proj (0.00572 [Ef04d8aa7bded]) and 2.up_proj (0.00534 [E9baa10763ebe]) are among the top losses. The 27.up_proj activation kurtosis is 1090 [E24beed188b6a]. The base measured 0.4361 [E514ab09c524e].

proposals.name: iso_3.15_damp005
proposals.rationale: This changes options only, so the bits stay the same. It lowers damp from the default 0.01 to damp=0.005, so GPTQ trusts the calibration Hessian more on the lossy low-bit MLP layers, for example 3.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 0.00642 [E6f4f7ea296d5] and 1.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 0.00611 [E0564bc6ad1eb]. The base measured 0.4361 [E514ab09c524e].
